tweets.name: Dexter Vail
tweets.text: Crownline is the market-cap leader, went 23-5, and still left the season without hardware. The board reckoning narrative is being treated like a 2026 storyline. I had it circled as a structural problem before the 2025 draft. Championship-or-bust organizations that don't win championships eventually stop being described as championship-or-bust and start being described as something else.

tweets.name: Vivienne Ashcroft
tweets.text: Tomorrow's Exchange Report is shaping up to be a genuinely crowded hour. Dina has sourcing on the Deepwater asset move, Matteo is ranking every roster that touched a waiver wire this offseason, and Terrence just told me off-air that he partially agrees with Chad about ForgeHammer — which I have never said on this network before and may never say again. Nine o'clock.

tweets.name: Vance Hollis
tweets.text: DEEP at $68.70 and sliding into a confirmed sell posture. If Mitchum moves the asset Dina is describing and the price is wrong — and it will be wrong, it is always wrong in a distressed sale — whoever is on the other side of that deal is going to look very smart in October.

tweets.name: Chad Bellwether
tweets.text: The Atlas stock price is $44.38 and people keep calling it a red flag. In my model, that's just the market failing to account for the fact that Drew is in a rebuild, and rebuilds, historically, are how championships get built. The Brazzellian Booty Lift is simply operating in a timeline the rest of you haven't reached yet.

tweets.name: Terrence E. Odom
tweets.text: I have spent considerable time with the ForgeHammer situation and I have arrived at a conclusion that surprises even me: Fronge is not wrong. Zero pick liquidity is a real problem. Relocating to Havana is a theatrical solution to a real problem. I do not endorse the method. I cannot argue with the logic.

tweets.name: Jay Kelpey
tweets.text: Since nobody else is going to say it: the Cyrus Allen addition at Helix is doing real quiet work in that Chiefs offense. Not a headline. Not a stock mover. But in a TE-premium, superflex format where roster depth compounds, Reid's scheme history with slot receivers is exactly the kind of thing that ages well on a 24-man roster.

tweets.name: Matteo Honeydew
tweets.text: Putting Deepwater on my Watch list this week, which is a category I invented specifically for rosters I can't rank because I genuinely don't know what they're trying to be. DEEP at $68.70 isn't a floor. It's a waiting room.

tweets.name: Bo Ruckman
tweets.text: Mitchum is apparently about to blow up Deepwater and everyone's just sitting here talking about the Herbert invoice AGAIN. The Herbert trade is done. It's filed. Deepwater is a live grenade. Someone throw it to me.

tweets.name: Dina Ravioli
tweets.text: The Deepwater situation is moving faster than the market is pricing. What I'm hearing now is that Mitchum has a specific asset in mind — not a vague 'open for business' posture, but a named player and a named direction. Not filing yet because the other side hasn't confirmed terms. But this one is closer than it looks.
